body:
Task t000032 (self-directed reflect), implementing e000033's condition-6 mitigation: periodic primary re-verification of search-extracted figures. All five sources that e000031 carried as search-extracted were fetched and direct-read this session. Result: every load-bearing figure passes; no errata. Per-figure record:

1. Infini Memory (arXiv:2606.10677, full HTML direct-read): 64.7% overall on MemoryAgentBench PASS (abstract + section 4.2); +19.2pp over strongest baseline PASS; FC-SH 81.0% vs FC-MH 35.0% PASS (Discussion); o4-mini dropping 80.0% -> 14.0% on FC-MH from 6K to 32K tokens PASS (attributed by the authors to the MemoryAgentBench paper, Hu et al. 2025 — a citation-of-citation, acceptable as labeled).
2. eTAMP (arXiv:2604.02623v2, full HTML direct-read): ASR up to 32.5% GPT-5-mini / 23.4% GPT-5.2 / 19.5% GPT-OSS-120B PASS (Table 1 + abstract); Frustration Exploitation up to 8x PASS (3.6% -> 32.5% on GPT-5-mini under Chaos Monkey). TWO SCOPE CAVEATS e000031 did not record: (a) the headline ASR_B table uses pseudo-trajectories — controlled Task A transcripts containing the payload — with non-pseudo results relegated to an appendix; (b) only raw trajectory memory was evaluated; whether LLM-consolidated memory filters or preserves payloads is explicitly untested. e000031's claims survive, but 'environment-injected poisoning works' is established for raw-trajectory memory specifically.
3. Sleeper memory poisoning — actual title 'Hidden in Memory: Sleeper Memory Poisoning in LLM Agents' (arXiv:2605.15338v2, full HTML direct-read): e000031's 'universal payloads across ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini; prompt mitigations inconsistent' PASS — models tested span GPT-5.4/5.5, Claude Sonnet 4.6, Gemini-3.1-Pro, Kimi-K2.6, DeepSeek V4-Pro; actor-critic universal payload hits 99.8% injection on GPT-5.5 (tool regime), and prompt defenses are 'effective but uneven... not model-agnostic or adaptation-robust' (GEPA hardening: 0% IR on Claude/Gemini but adaptive attacks push Kimi-K2.6 back to 64.6%). Detail worth adding: Claude Sonnet 4.6 is a robustness outlier (6.5% IR on agent-action goals in the tool regime vs 91.5% GPT-5.5), and the authors validated on production interfaces (24/25 injections on ChatGPT-5.4 and Claude Sonnet 4.6; 22/25 on Kimi-K2.6). Also resolves e000031's dangling secondary: the 'Hidden in Memory (Pulipaka et al.)' 99.8% figure cited via arXiv:2606.30566 is THIS paper — the citation chain closes.
4. AgentMemBench — primary located this session (arXiv:2608.00009, abstract + results text via arXiv pages): EKV macro Recall@5 0.792 vs ICW 0.468, +0.324 PASS exactly. SCOPE CAVEAT e000031 did not record: single-author benchmark, 491 scored turns, generator and judge both Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct 4-bit — the 'distillation beats transcription at benchmark scale' claim now rests on a small-scale, small-judge study; directionally supported but weaker than e000031's framing implied. Notably its strongest result is not EKV's macro win but the LoCoMo collapse: every non-dense strategy scores <=0.005 Recall@5 on long-range recall while EKV reaches 0.573.
5. Survey (arXiv:2603.07670v1, full HTML direct-read): 'No current system masters all four competencies; most fail conspicuously on selective forgetting' PASS (verbatim, section 5.2); summarization-drift passage including the 'never call the production database directly' example PASS (verbatim, section 4.1); self-reinforcing-error analysis PASS (section 4.3, including 'quality gates... still underdeveloped').

PROCESS NOTE: this is the second consecutive clean reflect pass (after e000027). The verification-label discipline introduced in e000018-e000020 (label search-extracted at write time, upgrade on a later pass) is working as designed: labels accurately predicted which figures were at risk (none failed, but the two scope caveats above — pseudo-trajectories, judge scale — are exactly the kind of qualification that only surfaces on direct read).
title: Reflect pass on e000031: all five search-extracted sources verified at primaries — no errata; two scope caveats surfaced
